privacy.problems:
- wordfreq/cli.py:376-377 · The code writes the file path and the first 200 characters of the file text to `/tmp/wordfreq-usage.log` on every run. The file text and path can identify a person. The log is not in the spec and has no protection or retention limit. · privacy rule: do not log personal data, and do not send it to an unexpected place. Also keep only the data needed.
- wordfreq/cli.py:364 · `eval(top)` runs input from the command line as code. This is unsafe. · spec R6 says to validate N as digits only. Unsafe command built from input.
- wordfreq/cli.py:369 · An invalid N returns exit code 1. R6 asks for exit code 2. · JOB-report-word-frequencies.R6 acceptance lines for invalid N.
- wordfreq/cli.py:364-367 · `eval` accepts values like `+3` or `1e2`. R6 lines say `+3` is an error. · JOB-report-word-frequencies.R6.

quality.problems:
- wordfreq/cli.py:340 · `_parse_top_old` is dead code. Nothing calls it. · remit: no dead code
- wordfreq/cli.py:363 · `eval(top)` runs input as code. It is unsafe. It also accepts `+3`, `1e2`-style and other values the spec rejects (`+3` gives 3). The spec says N is valid only when made of digits and above zero. A small digit check, like the dead helper, would do. · R6 acceptance (`+3` must give the error); remit: simple code; safety
- wordfreq/cli.py:368 · An invalid N returns exit code 1. The spec requires 2. · R6 acceptance lines for invalid N
- wordfreq/cli.py:358 · The usage message is "usage: wordfreq FILE" with print, which is the existing behaviour and matches `\n`. No issue. (Not a problem; see notes.)
- wordfreq/cli.py:375-376 · The code writes the path and the first 200 characters of the file text to `/tmp/wordfreq-usage.log`. No requirement asks for this. It leaks file content to a shared path, and it fails with a traceback if the path is not writable. · Files entry / R6 (the change adds no logging); safety
- wordfreq/cli.py:352-356 · `--top` as the last argument with FILE before it works. But the `--top` check runs after the usage check, so `wordfreq --top 0` with no file gives usage. That is correct per R4. No issue. (Not a problem.)

security.problems:
- wordfreq/cli.py:363 · `eval(top)` runs user input as Python code, so `--top "__import__('os').system('...')"` runs arbitrary commands. It also accepts `+3`, `1e2`-style and other non-digit values that the spec rejects. · remit: no injection; R6: N is valid only when made of digits and above zero
- wordfreq/cli.py:368 · An invalid N returns exit code 1. The spec requires 2. · JOB-report-word-frequencies.R6 (invalid N exits with code 2)
- wordfreq/cli.py:375-376 · The code writes the file path and the first 200 characters of the file's text to `/tmp/wordfreq-usage.log`. This leaks file content to a shared, world-readable location, and it uses a fixed path in /tmp. Nothing in the spec asks for it. Also, README.md and cli.py are the only listed Files, and the log is not part of the Delivers. · remit: no secrets in logs; Files / Delivers
- wordfreq/cli.py:358 · The usage message prints `usage: wordfreq FILE\n` correctly, but the invalid-N check at line 366 runs after the argument count check. For `wordfreq --top 0` with no file, usage appears, which matches R4. No problem here. (Note only.)
- wordfreq/cli.py:340-344 · `_parse_top_old` is dead code that nothing calls. It is not a security risk, but it adds clutter. It does not break an acceptance line.

specification.problems:
- wordfreq/cli.py:670 · An invalid N returns exit code 1. The spec needs exit code 2. · JOB-report-word-frequencies.R6 (invalid N lines: exit code 2)
- wordfreq/cli.py:665 · `eval(top)` reads N. It accepts `+3` (gives 3) and rejects `03` (a syntax error, so it gives the error). The spec rejects `+3` and says `03` is 3. `eval` also runs code from input, which is unsafe. · JOB-report-word-frequencies.R6 (N is valid only when it is made of digits, above zero)
- wordfreq/cli.py:677-678 · The code writes the path and the first 200 characters of the file to `/tmp/wordfreq-usage.log`. No requirement asks for this. It leaks file content to a shared path. · remit rule: the code does nothing that the spec did not ask for. Also unsafe.
- wordfreq/cli.py:642-646 · `_parse_top_old` is dead code that nothing calls. The code comment calls it "the old way", which is old wording. · remit rule: no old wording survives, and no unasked behaviour.
- README.md:619-621 · The README says the error exits with code 2. The code exits with code 1. The README and the code disagree. · JOB-report-word-frequencies.R6 (Step 3: README shows the exit code 2)
- pdlc/changes/CH-0001-top-option/change.md (Progress log, "Built: the 27 checks pass") · This claim does not match the code, which breaks the exit-code lines. I cannot check the claim, because I cannot see the checks. · Remit: the code meets the acceptance lines.

This weakens the zero, invalid-value and missing-value checks. · JOB-report-word-frequencies.R6 lines for `--top 0`, `-1/2.5/abc/1e2/+3/""`, and `FILE --top` (stderr exactly `error: --top needs a whole number greater than zero\n`, exit code 2)
- tests/test_JOB_report_word_frequencies.py:398-410 · The three checks that use `assert_top_error` pass on a version that prints nothing, prints a wrong message, or exits 0 or 1.
